reason:
Reproduced exactly at 1440x960, state=owner-editing. The edited row 'Send the invitations' sits at viewport y=696; +7 puts it at 822, then 948, 1074, 1200, and window.scrollY stays 0 through every press while the viewport is 960 tall. keepInBand() returns early because it is gated on the panel being position:fixed and at >=1024 .b-edit computes to relative, so nothing follows the move. The owner is holding a control whose only job is to slide a thing along a scale, and the thing is off the bottom of the scale from the second press on. The behaviour gate does NOT cover this: interaction-check.mjs asserts 'the move is on screen where it happens' only at 390 and 768, so this is the hole that assertion leaves, not a restatement of it.

The round-7 refusal does not reach this fix, and I measured that rather than taking the seat's word for it. Round 7 refused scrolling the WINDOW, on the ground that .b-stick drifts ~191px and then unsticks, seating Delete under a repeat-press point. I confirmed that drift is real and pre-existing (base at 1280x800: the stepper moves 829 -> 638 the moment the page scrolls). This fix moves the right column instead. Prototyped by injecting max-height/overflow-y:auto on the second child of .b-two and bringing the row into view inside it AFTER the move settles: at 1440x960 through four presses scrollY stays 0, the +7 stepper stays at y=829 pixel-for-pixel, Delete stays at 1100, and the row stays inside the rail (bottom 935 against a rail bottom of 936). Same at 1280x900. Nothing in the left column moves by a pixel, so the objection that killed round 7's version has nothing to bite on. Document height also drops 2130 -> 1329 at 1440. The undo-bar gate at 1440 and 1280 is untouched, because the bar lives in the left column and the left column is byte-identical before and after.

The fix as WORDED is wrong in four places and must be sharpened, but every one of them is an implementation detail, not a reason the direction fails. Confirmed on the direction, with the corrections below.
sharpenedFix:
Four corrections, all measured:

1. Do NOT call scrollIntoView after place() in the same frame. The move is a CSS transition, so getBoundingClientRect returns the mid-flight position, and the scroll lands 126px short every press. Prototyped literally as written, the row parks at viewport 970..1061 against a rail bottom of 936 and never re-enters the rail for four presses running - i.e. the fix as specified does not fix the defect. The codebase already solved this once: keepInBand computes where the row WILL be arithmetically instead of reading it. Do the same here - compute the destination top from the new data-away and px-per-day and assign scroller.scrollTop directly, or defer past transitionend. Also note scrollIntoView has no 'against that scroller rather than the window' mode; it walks every scrollable ancestor. Setting scrollTop is what actually guarantees the window does not move.

2. Scope it. .b-two is also the audience 'desk' state and the print sheet, where the whole composition is a page that scrolls as one; a nested scroller there is wrong. Gate the rule on [data-medium="full"] .b-ownerField, or give the owner's right column its own class.

3. Drop overscroll-behavior: contain. It buys nothing here and costs real reach: the rail is 668px of a 1440 viewport (46%), while Done sits at document y 1036 and Delete at 1100 with a 960-tall viewport and only ~370px of page scroll left. Contain means a wheel over nearly half the screen never reaches the two controls that end the edit. Let it chain.

4. Rewire the horizon's gap sentence, which the finding does not mention and which this fix breaks. .b-gapNote listens on window scroll and picks the first row whose viewport top >= 0. Measured under the prototype: after scrolling the rail 600px the sentence is stale ('Nothing is planned until 1 August'), and when it does recompute, viewport-relative picks 'Send the invitations' while the rail actually shows 'Final dress fitting' - the horizon would name a row clipped out of view. Add the scroller to the same listener and compare each row against the scroller's rect, not against 0.
